data.summary: Richardson, Hu, Moss, and Sabharwal propose semantic fragments to probe NLI models' reasoning on logic, monotonicity, and quantification. State-of-the-art models like BERT perform poorly on these fragments despite centrality to NLI. With brief finetuning and inoculation, a BERT-based model masters all logic and monotonicity fragments while retaining established benchmark performance.
data.limitations:
The source authors state: "In the case of comparatives, the inability of the model to master this fragment likely
reveals a certain architectural limitation of the model given

that it is not sensitive to word-order."
data.abstract: Richardson, Hu, Moss, and Sabharwal propose semantic fragments—systematically generated NLI datasets each targeting a distinct semantic phenomenon—for probing, and efficiently improving, such capabilities of linguistic models.
data.introduction: Richardson, Hu, Moss, and Sabharwal propose semantic fragments to investigate the extent to which state-of-the-art NLI models capture central semantic phenomena.
data.conclusion: With only a few minutes of additional finetuning, a BERT-based model can master all of these logic and monotonicity fragments while retaining its performance on established NLI benchmarks.
